name: evtx_query
description: Query an EVTX event log and return filtered events with timestamp, event id, channel, computer, provider, EventRecordID and named data fields. A run reports three counts apart: records_examined (every record the reader produced), events_matched (records that parsed and passed every filter) and parse_errors (records or chunk chains that could not be read, with their offsets); an error row is never counted as a match, and a run with any parse error, or whose chunks could not be enumerated to the end, is status partial. Every row carries record_offset, chunk_offset, the EventRecordID and record_filetime (the FILETIME in the record header, as a decimal string, with record_time_utc by integer arithmetic) beside the XML's own SystemTime. Filters: event_ids, contains (a substring of the XML), start_record and end_record, and start_time and end_time (ISO 8601: YYYY-MM-DD then optionally THH, THH:MM, THH:MM:SS or THH:MM:SS.fffffff, and from the hour on Z or an offset such as +03:00; no zone is UTC; a time names the span its precision gives, so a date is the whole day; the SystemTime of each record is converted to UTC ticks and compared as a number; a malformed time, a word such as yesterday, or a range that ends before it starts is refused; a record with no SystemTime is left out of a time range and counted in events_without_time_excluded, and the run is partial). The log is accounted for as a whole: chunks_declared (what the file header says), chunks_read (what the reader gave), bytes_expected and file_bytes; a file shorter than its header says or a reader that gave fewer chunks than declared is status partial with a problem naming both, not a log with no records. The XML of every match is kept in the result file (JSON Lines), which is created exclusively and never replaces or truncates an earlier result: when the name is taken the first free -2, -3... beside it is used and result_file_requested says so; its default name is made from the arguments without `contains`, so a needle never reaches a file name. limit is the inline page size. SENSITIVE: event data can hold command lines and text typed into one, which can hold a secret; run it as a job with secret_output: true when the log may.

event_ids.description: Optional list of numeric event IDs to include

contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring that must appear in the XML

limit.description: Events shown inline (default 200, an inline page size); every matching event and its whole XML is kept in result_file, and parse-error rows are listed under errors and kept there too

out_file.description: Optional JSONL result path under the run (in a job, under $OUT); defaults to work/<your id>/tool-output/ (in a job, $OUT). An existing file is never replaced: the first free name beside it is used and named

start_time.description: Optional ISO 8601 lower bound on the XML's SystemTime: the beginning of the span the text names (2026-09-01 is 00:00 that day, 2026-09-01T10:00 is 10:00:00); no zone is UTC, Z or an offset is applied

end_time.description: Optional ISO 8601 upper bound on the XML's SystemTime: the end of the span the text names, so 2026-09-01 includes the whole day and 2026-09-01T10:00 that whole minute; no zone is UTC, Z or an offset is applied
